name: @dudo/web
description: Dudo responsive web application — React SPA on Cloudflare Workers Static Assets (ADR 0016)

scripts.//verify:kdf MOVED 2026-09-09: The KDF and its suite are `@dudo/client-kdf` (ADR 0040 step 4). Run it with `npm run verify:kdf --workspace packages/client-kdf`. The suite that lives there is the UNION of the two this console and platform/admin carried separately — 17 assertions were present in one and absent from the other.
scripts.//smoke: Loads the BUILT application in a headless browser and drives it. IT IS THE ONLY INSTRUMENT IN THIS REPOSITORY THAT SEES COMPOSITION. Everything else inspects source or types, and on 2026-09-09 in platform/admin `tsc` exited 0, `vite build` exited 0 and `npm run verify` reported 584 passing assertions ON A BLANK PAGE — a circular import, which is a property of the import graph rather than of any file. In this package it has caught: a submit button that did nothing at all on an empty form (typechecked, built, silent), a dead `href="#/customers"` on the header wordmark that 57 other checks passed straight over because none clicked the logo, and one of its own assertions passing for the wrong reason. RUN IT AFTER `npm run build` — it drives `vite preview` over `dist/`, so it reports on the last build rather than on the working tree. FOUR STATES, CARRIED BY THE EXIT CODE: 0 passed, 1 failed, 2 NOT RUN because no browser is installed. 2 IS NEITHER A PASS NOR A SKIP.
scripts.//WHY smoke IS NOT IN `verify`: It needs a browser on the machine, and a gate that depends on what is installed reports on the machine rather than on the code. It is run by name, and it joins `verify` the day it can be relied on everywhere — the same condition `check:source-bytes` was held to. NO DEPENDENCY IS ADDED BY IT: it uses whatever Chromium-based browser is already present and exits 2, loudly, when there is none.
scripts.//check:ui-purity MOVED 2026-09-09: It now lives in `packages/ui` and covers `@dudo/ui` ALONE (ADR 0040 step 3). It is NOT pointed at a second directory as well, and that was deliberate: this console no longer has a primitive layer to guard, and guarding two would bless two separate layers as correct when the entire purpose of the package is that there should be one. Run it with `npm run check:ui-purity --workspace packages/ui`. The constraint it enforces — that the shared layer carries no authority — had never been tested by anything before the package existed, because it was aimed at one host's private directory and there was no shared component for the rule to apply to.
scripts.//check:suite-parity RETIRED 2026-09-09: RETIRED BECAUSE ITS SUBJECT IS GONE, NOT BECAUSE IT BECAME INCONVENIENT — the `//check:contracts` precedent at the root. It compared the `check(...)` labels of two verify-kdf suites; ADR 0040 unioned them into one file in `@dudo/client-kdf`, so there are no longer two things to compare and 'they agree' is trivially true. RECORDING WHAT IT CAUGHT, because a retired check that lists its findings teaches and one that just disappears does not. (1) SEVENTEEN REAL GAPS — 16 assertions present in web and absent from admin, 1 the reverse — closed by ADDING ASSERTIONS, never by widening the exemption list. Among them the PRINTABLE-ASCII BOUNDARY on `isSubmittableIdentifier` (DEL 0x7F refused, tilde 0x7E accepted), asserted on one console's login path and not the other's; and `returned email is normalised`, asserted on NEITHER — if that address were ever returned un-normalised the client would salt with one string and send another, and every sign-in would be refused with nothing in the response able to explain it. (2) A MISLABELLED ASSERTION: admin carried web's fresh-derivation LABEL over a published-vector COMPARISON. Byte-identity would have flagged the wording and missed the substance; label-set equality found it. (3) AN EXEMPTION THAT RETIRED ITSELF: `DEL is U+007F` was listed host-specific, stopped being true the moment admin spelled the constant, and was removed rather than defended. Its entry also carried the refusal 'the DEL TEST ITSELF is NOT exempt and must not be added here' — WRITTEN AT THE POINT OF TEMPTATION, MET BY THE PERSON TEMPTED, AND HONOURED. The gap was closed by adding the assertion, which is the outcome the refusal existed to force. That is the guard-where-the-hand-goes technique completing a full cycle, and it is the strongest evidence in this repository that it works. (4) A DEFECT IN ITSELF on its first run: it read a JSDoc line demonstrating how to import and reported it as an import. Comments are stripped now, floor-tested. THE SCRIPT IS DELETED; this entry is the record.
scripts.verify: npm run typecheck && npm run verify:transport && npm run verify:auth && npm run verify:organization && npm run verify:search-params

//dependencies: EVERY VERSION IS EXACT. No ^, no ~, anywhere in this file.
ADR 0036 requires it of the six libraries it approved; the pre-existing five were
pinned in the same pass so the rule is a property of the file rather than of one
commit. Pinning changed no resolved version — each value is what the lockfile
already resolved, so `npm ci` and `npm install` now agree by construction instead
THE APPROVED SET (user, 2026-09-08) IS: shadcn/ui, TanStack Router, TanStack Query,
TanStack Table, React Hook Form, Zod. shadcn/ui is copy-in source and is therefore
NOT LISTED HERE and never will be (ADR 0016 §2). A seventh library is a new user
approval, not a judgement call — see docs/decisions/0036 and security.md §7.
NO RADIX PACKAGE IS INSTALLED YET, and that is deliberate rather than an omission.
0036 named Radix as arriving transitively under shadcn/ui so the count would be
honest; nothing in this repository copies in a shadcn component that needs it yet.
It arrives with the first real dialog or menu, which is already covered by the same
approval and needs no new one.
